The $2$nd row of the given matrix contains two zeros, more than any other row. So, using a Laplace expansion along the $2$nd row, we have   

$$\begin{aligned}\begin{vmatrix}0 & 1 & 2 & -1 \\ {\color{red}0} & {\color{red}-1} & {\color{red}0} & {\color{red}1} \\ 2 & 3 & 1 & 1 \\ 2 & 0 & -3 & 3\end{vmatrix} & ={\color{red}0}\cdot {\color{black}{C}_{21}}+{\color{red}(-1)}\cdot {\color{blue}{C}_{22}}+{\color{red}0}\cdot {\color{black}{C}_{23}}+{\color{red}1}\cdot {\color{blue}{C}_{24}} \\  & ={\color{red}(-1)}\cdot {\color{blue}(-1)^{2+2}\cdot \begin{vmatrix}0 & 2 & -1 \\ 2 & 1 & 1 \\ 2 & -3 & 3\end{vmatrix}}+{\color{red}1}\cdot {\color{blue}(-1)^{2+4}\cdot \begin{vmatrix}0 & 1 & 2 \\ 2 & 3 & 1 \\ 2 & 0 & -3\end{vmatrix}} \\  & =-\begin{vmatrix}0 & 2 & -1 \\ 2 & 1 & 1 \\ 2 & -3 & 3\end{vmatrix}+\begin{vmatrix}0 & 1 & 2 \\ 2 & 3 & 1 \\ 2 & 0 & -3\end{vmatrix}.\end{aligned}$$

Now, computing the first $3\times 3$  determinant by applying a Laplace expansion along the $1$st row, we obtain:

$$\begin{aligned}\begin{vmatrix}{\color{red}0} & {\color{red}2} & {\color{red}-1} \\ 2 & 1 & 1 \\ 2 & -3 & 3\end{vmatrix} & ={\color{red}0}\cdot {\color{black}{C}_{11}}+{\color{red}2}\cdot {\color{blue}{C}_{12}}+{\color{red}(-1)}\cdot {\color{blue}{C}_{13}} \\  & ={\color{red}2}\cdot {\color{blue}(-1)^{1+2}\cdot \begin{vmatrix}2 & 1 \\ 2 & 3\end{vmatrix}}+{\color{red}(-1)}\cdot {\color{blue}(-1)^{1+3}\cdot \begin{vmatrix}2 & 1 \\ 2 & -3\end{vmatrix}} \\  & =-2\begin{vmatrix}2 & 1 \\ 2 & 3\end{vmatrix}-\begin{vmatrix}2 & 1 \\ 2 & -3\end{vmatrix} \\  & =-2(6-2)-(-6-2) \\  & =-8-(-8) \\  & =0\end{aligned}$$

Finally, we compute the second $3\times 3$ determinant by applying a Laplace expansion along the $1$st row:

$$\begin{aligned}\begin{vmatrix}{\color{red}0} & {\color{red}1} & {\color{red}2} \\ 2 & 3 & 1 \\ 2 & 0 & -3\end{vmatrix} & ={\color{red}0}\cdot {\color{black}{C}_{11}}+{\color{red}1}\cdot {\color{blue}{C}_{12}}+{\color{red}2}\cdot {\color{blue}{C}_{13}} \\  & ={\color{red}1}\cdot {\color{blue}(-1)^{1+2}\cdot \begin{vmatrix}2 & 1 \\ 2 & -3\end{vmatrix}}+{\color{red}(2)}\cdot {\color{blue}(-1)^{1+3}\cdot \begin{vmatrix}2 & 3 \\ 2 & 0\end{vmatrix}} \\  & =-\begin{vmatrix}2 & 1 \\ 2 & -3\end{vmatrix}+2\begin{vmatrix}2 & 3 \\ 2 & 0\end{vmatrix} \\  & =-(-6-2)+2(0-6) \\  & =-(-8)+2\cdot (-6) \\  & =8-12 \\  & =-4\end{aligned}$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{vmatrix}0 & 1 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & -1 & 0 & 1 \\ 2 & 3 & 1 & 1 \\ 2 & 0 & -3 & 3\end{vmatrix}=-0+(-4)=-4.
$$
